card.name: Linking verbs before hedged drug statements
card.fires_on: The word "is", "which" or a noun like "activity" right after a drug-interaction or overdose subject, just before a hedge or recommendation such as "not recommended", "unlikely" or "may result".

modes.label: "is" before a verdict
modes.description: The verb "is" after a subject like overdose, dialysis or concomitant use, ahead of "not recommended" or "unlikely".
modes.example: Concomitant use with alcohol<< is>> not recommended, as it may increase the

modes.label: "which" after an exposure change
modes.description: The relative word "which" after a statement of changed drug exposure, ahead of "may result" or "may increase".
modes.example: CYP2C8 inducers (e.g., rifampin) may decrease daprodustat exposure,<< which>> may result in loss of efficacy.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward hedging adverbs such as "likely", "potentially" and "probably", and away from words like "effective".
card.plain: It marks the spot in an interaction or overdose sentence where a hedged or cautious conclusion is about to follow.
